summary: Team management (the manager's view of their team)
description: A manager sees their direct reports as a team (My Team) and can open one person to review all of their requests with filters. Team Approvals stays the fast pending inbox. Decided 2026-10-18: a My Team area (roster, then a page per person); the employee's free-text reason only on pending requests; the roster shows out today or next leave, pending count, Vacation and Sick days left and the last request; design (a mockup) before the UI tasks; build after the 2026-10-19 demo. Each slice has its own PRD story and task.

summary: My Team roster query (scoped to direct reports)
description: One SQL statement (u.manager_id = the session user's id, in the query itself, never filtered in TypeScript) returning one row per direct report: name; out today (an approved request covers today in APP_TIMEZONE) or the start of the next approved leave; pending request count; available Vacation and Sick days after pending (same rules as summarizeBalances); the most recent non-deleted request and its status. Never the caller, never another team. At most POOL_MAX - 1 parallel statements for the page (one statement here). Tests: Leo (another team) never appears, the manager is not in their own roster, an empty team, exact figures, a real-engine integration test on a fresh database with a break-the-filter proof.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: only the caller's direct reports, one row each, in name order, never the caller or another team (Leo);AC2: each row carries out-today or next approved leave, the pending count, available Vacation and Sick after pending and the latest request with its status;AC3: a manager with no reports gets an empty list, not an error;AC4: the scope is in the SQL and a request from another team never changes any figure;AC5: one statement for the page (query budget test stays green)

summary: My Team page, navigation item and role guard
description: Server page /approvals/team, the My team tab of Team Approvals (requireRole manager and hr_admin; an employee is sent to /dashboard), no sidebar item of its own: the Team Approvals item stays highlighted and a shared tab bar links Approvals and My team, the roster UI from the agreed design (a mockup first), empty and error states, a skeleton and loading.tsx that mirror the page, mobile first (nothing horizontal at 375 and 320 px), status written as text, tokens only. Each row links to /approvals/team/[person] (TASK-036). Read through src/lib/leave/* directly (AGENTS.md rule 11).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a manager and an HR Admin see the My team tab under Team Approvals, an employee does not see Team Approvals and is redirected;AC2: the roster shows the fields of US-12 AC2 and links each person to their page;AC3: an empty team shows an empty state;AC4: a failed read says so with a way to retry and the rest of the app works;AC5: no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px and nothing is shown by colour alone

summary: Team member history query: scope, filters and pagination
description: A read module for one direct report. The person comes from the URL and is NEVER trusted: the SQL checks u.manager_id = the session user's id in the same statement, and another team's member, a missing person and a deleted one all give the same not found (no existence leak). A zod schema for the filters in the page address (leave type, status, year within the last three years, page; an invalid value must not cause a server error). Returns the person's balances (confirmed, pending, available after pending; same figures as My Balance), the matching non-deleted requests (newest start date first, a request counts in every year it overlaps, 25 per page) and the total. The employee's free-text reason is selected only for pending requests, in the SQL, so it can never reach a decided row. At most POOL_MAX - 1 parallel statements. Tests: Leo, a missing and a deleted person give the same result, the reason never appears on a decided request, every filter, the year clip, pagination, a real-engine test with a break-the-filter proof.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the person's balances and non-deleted requests, newest start date first;AC2: filters by leave type, status and year (default current year, last three years allowed);AC3: an invalid filter value never causes a server error;AC4: the reason is returned only for pending requests;AC5: a person outside the caller's team, a missing and a deleted person give the same not found and no data;AC6: 25 per page with the total count;AC7: scoped in the SQL, one statement per read, query budget stays green

summary: Team member page: balances, filters, requests and decisions
description: Server page /approvals/team/[userId] from the agreed design: the person's name and balances, a Filters card (selects for leave type, status and year with icons, Apply filters, Clear filters, and a chip per applied filter that removes just that filter; the choices live in the address, applying them updates only the results by client navigation without a full page reload, and the form is a plain GET form without JavaScript), the requests as a real table from sm and stacked rows below it (the My Balance pattern, no table display switching), 25 per page with next and previous and the match count, the existing Approve and Reject component and POST /api/leave-requests/:id/decision for pending rows (the same rules as Team Approvals, audited), a uniform not found page, error and empty states, a skeleton and loading.tsx. Mobile first; status written as text; tokens only; no client code beyond the existing approval actions.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: balances and all requests with filters as in US-13 AC1 to AC3;AC2: pending requests can be approved or rejected here with the same rules as Team Approvals;AC3: decided requests never show the employee's reason, a rejection's note always shows;AC4: a person outside the team shows the same not found as a missing person;AC5: pagination and the match count;AC6: a failed read says so with a way to retry;AC7: no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px
